last_session.detail: The party assumed the treasure lies at one of the marked locations, but all the land around Brandonsford was unknown to them.
last_session.text: The party arrived in Brandonsford at sunset, following a treasure map whose marked places no one recognized.

last_session.detail: Reginald said the Clurichen is up to no good and that wherever it goes, they should stay away.
last_session.text: Reginald the frog warned Dr. Uriah that a trickster Clurichen comes into town from the riverbanks every night.

last_session.detail: Dunk left the party to scavenge, preferring solitude to the inns. Gill's legend: Sir Brandon got a magic sword from a fairy in the woods, and he and his friends killed a dragon that had terrorized the town for weeks. The town was named after him. They were knighted and left, and Brandon died. That dragon was dragged through town and ripped apart hundreds of years ago. Gill assumes the current dragon is a different one and does not know where dragons come from. Gill saw the current dragon, which wanted nothing to do with him. Dunk asked to sleep in the barn and think over Gill's offer; they drank from Gill's still while Gill shared gossip.
last_session.text: Dunk spent the night drinking with Farmer Gill, who told him the legend of Sir Brandon and his dragon.

last_session.detail: Eric said the dragon was the first of many problems he has. He said George, a capable woodsman living a couple of houses down, lost an arm to the dragon, which George described as a black dragon, not a big one. Sir Phidipaldi slapped Eric with his glove when Eric defended George's account; the flustered Eric did not accept the duel, only saying Sir Phidipaldi was more skilled at adventure.
last_session.text: Eric the Reeve offered 1000 gold for the dragon, and Sir Phidipaldi slapped him and challenged him to a duel.

last_session.detail: Uriah brought him a Fox Tail Brew; Ned recognized Uriah as a Dagonite. Uriah said he was a scholar of folk remedies and lore looking for work with his crew. For a night of at least ten kills, Ned would keep the fee but pay back 5 gold per kill if he could do what he wanted with the victims.
last_session.text: Drop Dead Ned, a thief with a killer wasp, offered to hire on with Dr. Uriah, who said he would think about it.

last_session.detail: Quinn says his good stock is gone each morning, with half the glasses empty or knocked over, so he waters down what is left. He believes Bentley steals it because Bentley's Fox Tail Brew is so popular. Quinn offered 100 gold and proposed a fake shipment.
last_session.text: Sir Phidipaldi agreed to help Quinn, who keeps the Golden Egg, catch whoever empties his ale each night.

open.text: Find the treasure shown on the party's map.

open.detail: The party never explicitly accepted Eric's offer; Sir Phidipaldi said they would talk to the Reeve, then denied the dragon exists and challenged Eric to a duel.
open.text: Kill the black dragon and drag its body into town to collect Eric the Reeve's 1000 gold.
Catch whoever empties Quinn's good ale at the Golden Egg each night and collect his 100 gold.

open.detail: Lady Hilda is a seasoned fighter in chain mail with a shield.
open.text: If the party pays Lady Hilda, she will join them to hunt the dragon. She won't go alone.

open.detail: Dr. Uriah said he would think about the offer.
open.text: If Dr. Uriah pays Drop Dead Ned 100 gold a week, Ned and his killer wasp will work for him. Ned insists on killing people.

open.detail: Quinn brings bottles, they fill them with water, and Sir Phidipaldi makes a big show of delivering ale.
open.text: If Sir Phidipaldi and Quinn stage their fake ale delivery, they may see who comes for the ale.
